handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

m2_scope.what_is_m2: Knowledge pack — derive reusable patterns from the case library for use by System B at inference time. Output is a machine-readable JSON plus a human-reviewable markdown doc.
output_files: phase1/knowledge_pack/knowledge_pack.json — patterns for System B to load into context
phase1/knowledge_pack/patterns_review.md — human-readable summary for Nolan to sanity-check
m2_scope.script_to_build: phase1/knowledge_pack/derive_patterns.py — reads from phase1/case_library/*.json, outputs the above.

components.dollar_per_unit_distributions: For each line item description/category: median $/unit, min, max, std, job count, date range. Segmented by job_type where data supports it. Only items with non-LS units get meaningful $/unit (LF, EA, SY, SF, CY). LS items recorded as $/job for reference. Source: proposals[primary].line_items across all 11 jobs with proposals.
components.derivation_rules: Rules that let System B fill gaps when a sheet doesn't show a quantity. Key rules to derive: (1) sewer_services = lot_count [check all jobs], (2) water_services = lot_count [check all jobs], (3) driveways = lot_count [check all jobs], (4) fire_hydrants ~ road_LF/500 [rough rule], (5) sewer_manholes ~ sewer_LF/250. Express each rule as {formula, observed_support: 'N/M jobs', confidence}.
components.typical_section_defaults: Stripping depth and ROW_SF/road_LF ratio (implied ROW width) per job type. Already in qty sheet scale_metrics for 8 jobs. Median stripping depth for subdivision_road. ROW width = ROW_SF / road_LF for each job.
components.job_type_signatures: For subdivision_road (the dominant type): dollar_per_lot range, dollar_per_road_LF range, dollar_per_ROW_SF range, characteristic line item categories present. For private_drive: same. Used by System B to sanity-check the total.
components.temporal_index: All $/unit values date-tagged with proposal_date. For M2, just record the dates — do not apply adjustments yet. Flag which items have enough observations (N>=3) for reliable medians.

open_questions: 6th Ave and Boyds Landing have no client_location in the manifest — job location unknown. Does it matter for M2 grouping? Probably not yet (too few non-Hayden-ID jobs to segment geographically).

Forest Grove PH2 proposal is from 2023 (oldest in the set) and includes a 9% sales tax on TAXED items (~$31k delta). The line_items_sum ($914,612) is pre-tax and is what's used for total_reconciled. Is the pre-tax total the right comparison for M2 $/unit, or should we use the grand total? Recommendation: use pre-tax (line_items_sum) to keep $/unit consistent across jobs.
6th Ave job_type is listed as 'subdivision_road' but Gemini noted it uses a private road (Davis Ln). Worth confirming — affects job_type_signature grouping.
Raghorn Estates has no proposal — scale metrics only. It contributes to lot_count/road_LF distributions but not $/unit. That's fine for M2.
